We need to propose a retrosynthesis route with 3 reactions for target SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

We have guidance: three steps: (1) amide formation from carboxylic acid + amine (coupling). (2) Doebner modification to form α,β-unsaturated acid from aromatic aldehyde + malonic acid. (3) sulfonamide formation from amine + sulfonyl chloride.

Thus retrosynthesis: target -> disconnect amide bond between C(=O)N and aniline (c3ccccc3N). So precursor 1: aromatic aldehyde? Wait amide formation step: product is amide linking the unsaturated acid (C=C-CO-NH-aryl). So break amide: gives acid (α,β-unsaturated carboxylic acid) and aniline (c3ccccc3N). The acid part includes the double bond and sulfonyl phenyl etc.

Next, the unsaturated acid can be derived via Doebner modification from aromatic aldehyde (the phenyl ring attached to sulfonyl) and malonic acid. The aldehyde is the phenyl ring with sulfonyl attached? Actually the unsaturated acid is /C=C/C(=O)N-aryl. The double bond attached to aromatic ring (c2ccc(... )cc2). So the aldehyde precursor would be the same aromatic ring with sulfonyl attached but with aldehyde at the position where the double bond will be formed (i.e., c2ccc(CHO)cc2 attached to sulfonyl). So precursor: aromatic aldehyde bearing sulfonyl group: c2ccc(CHO)cc2 attached to sulfonyl (SO2). So we need sulfonyl chloride to make sulfonamide later.

Third step: sulfonamide formation: attach sulfonyl chloride (SO2Cl) to aniline (the first phenyl ring with methyl). So precursor: aniline (para-methyl aniline) and sulfonyl chloride (SO2Cl attached to aromatic ring). The sulfonyl chloride is derived from the aromatic ring (c2ccc(SO2Cl)cc2). So we need to generate that from the aldehyde? Actually the aldehyde we have is c2ccc(CHO)cc2 attached to sulfonyl? Wait sulfonyl chloride is attached to aromatic ring, not the aldehyde. The sulfonyl chloride is the same aromatic ring as the aldehyde but with SO2Cl instead of SO2- attached to the other phenyl. So we need to have sulfonyl chloride as a reagent, not derived.

Thus retrosynthesis steps:

Step 1 (retro): amide bond cleavage -> gives α,β-unsaturated carboxylic acid (A) and aniline (B). B is c3ccccc3N (aniline). A is (E)-4-(sulfonyl phenyl)-cinnamic acid? Actually structure: /C=C/C(=O)N-aryl. So acid part: c2ccc(/C=C/COOH)cc2 attached to SO2? Wait the sulfonyl is attached to the phenyl ring (c2ccc(... )cc2) via NSO2 linking to first phenyl. In target, NS(=O)(=O) attached to first phenyl (methyl phenyl) and to second phenyl (c2...). So the sulfonamide is between first phenyl amine and sulfonyl group attached to second phenyl. So after amide cleavage, we still have sulfonamide present. So A still contains sulfonyl attached to second phenyl and the unsaturated acid side chain. So A is: c2ccc(SO2NH-? wait sulfonamide is between first phenyl and sulfonyl, so after cleavage, the sulfonamide remains attached to second phenyl? Actually the sulfonamide is NS(=O)(=O) attached to first phenyl (as N) and to second phenyl (as S). So the N is part of sulfonamide, attached to first phenyl. The second phenyl is attached to S. So after amide cleavage, the N of sulfonamide remains attached to first phenyl, not part of A. So A is the second phenyl with sulfonyl attached to N? Wait the sulfonyl group is attached to N on one side and to aromatic carbon on other side (S attached to aromatic carbon). So the sulfonamide nitrogen is the same as the amine that later forms sulfonamide. So in retrosynthesis, we could first disconnect sulfonamide formation: break S-N bond to give sulfonyl chloride (aryl-SO2Cl) and aniline (methyl phenyl amine). Then we have sulfonyl chloride attached to second phenyl. Then we need to attach that sulfonyl chloride to the first phenyl amine later (step 3 forward). So retro step 3: break sulfonamide -> gives aniline (first phenyl) and sulfonyl chloride (aryl-SO2Cl). Good.

Now we have remaining molecule after removing sulfonamide: we have second phenyl with sulfonyl chloride attached, and the unsaturated amide side chain attached to that phenyl via the double bond? Actually the unsaturated side chain is attached to the second phenyl at para position relative to sulfonyl? In target, the second phenyl has the side chain /C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N attached at para position relative to sulfonyl? The SMILES: NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2. So the sulfonyl attached to the first phenyl N, then S attached to aromatic carbon of second phenyl (c2). That second phenyl also has the side chain /C=C/C(=O)N-aryl attached. So after breaking sulfonamide, we have sulfonyl chloride attached to second phenyl (SO2Cl) and the side chain still attached to that phenyl. So the fragment is: c2ccc(SO2Cl)cc2 with side chain /C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N attached. That's the precursor for step 2 (Doebner) to generate the side chain unsaturated acid? Actually the side chain includes amide to aniline; that amide will be formed later (step 1). So after breaking amide, we have unsaturated acid attached to second phenyl (c2ccc(SO2Cl)cc2) with COOH at the end of double bond. So the fragment after amide cleavage is: c2ccc(SO2Cl)cc2-CH=CH-COOH (cinnamic acid derivative). That's the product of Doebner modification from aldehyde (c2ccc(SO2Cl)cc2-CHO) and malonic acid. So retro step 2: break C=C bond and form aldehyde + malonic acid. So we get aldehyde precursor: c2ccc(SO2Cl)cc2-CHO (aryl aldehyde with sulfonyl chloride). Good.

Thus overall retrosynthesis:

Target (T) -> step1 retro amide cleavage -> precursor A (aryl sulfonyl phenyl with cinnamic acid) + aniline (c3ccccc3N). (But aniline is separate, will be used later for amide formation.)

Step2 retro Doebner -> precursor B: aryl aldehyde with sulfonyl chloride (c2ccc(SO2Cl)cc2-CHO) + malonic acid (we can assume malonic acid is a simple reagent, not needed to list). (The side chain unsaturated acid derived.)

Step3 retro sulfonamide formation -> precursor C: aniline (first phenyl with methyl) (i.e., p-toluidine) and sulfonyl chloride (c2ccc(SO2Cl)cc2-CHO). Wait sulfonyl chloride is same as in step2, so step3 splits sulfonamide: gives p-toluidine (Cc1ccc(N)cc1) and sulfonyl chloride (c2ccc(SO2Cl)cc2-CHO). Actually the sulfonyl chloride already contains aldehyde; but after step2 we need aldehyde to undergo Doebner, so the sulfonyl chloride must have aldehyde. So step3 yields p-toluidine and aryl sulfonyl chloride aldehyde.

Thus final three steps forward:

1) Sulfonamide formation: p-toluidine + aryl sulfonyl chloride (with aldehyde) -> sulfonamide intermediate (aryl-sulfonyl-aryl with aldehyde side chain).

2) Doebner modification: aldehyde + malonic acid -> α,β-unsaturated carboxylic acid (cinnamic acid derivative) attached to sulfonyl phenyl.

3) Amide coupling: carboxylic acid + aniline (c3ccccc3N) -> final product.

We need to provide JSON route with three reaction nodes.

We need template IDs for each reaction. We have template 401931 which seems to be amide formation (amide from acid and amine). That template matches our target? It was found earlier with product containing amide and double bond. So we can use template_id 401931 for step 1 (forward amide formation). For sulfonamide formation, need a template that forms sulfonamide from amine and sulfonyl chloride. Search maybe. Let's search for sulfonamide formation.
